assembly_notes:
IDENTITY. A grounded low box housing carrying a bordered glass stage; a vertical mast rising from its rear-right corner on a prismatic slide; an optical head on the mast; and a mirror articulating above the head. Four mechanisms are present in every seed: the mast height slide, the head motion, one or two mirror hinges, and two body-mounted controls. The frame convention is +Z up, housing on the ground at z=0, -Y the operator side, mast at +X/+Y. The mast slide and every yoke swivel are on (0,0,1); every head and mirror tilt is on (0,1,0); both body controls are on (1,0,0). No joint anywhere in the 11-record pool uses any other axis, which is what makes the category machine-checkable.

DOMAIN ARITHMETIC. core_domain = 4 post_topology x 3 head_form x 3 focus x 4 mirror_motion x 1 body_controls = 144 combinations, every one of which must build. raw_domain = 144 as well, because this category has NO multiplicity axis (see below). Palette, continuous proportions (head_reach_m, mirror panel size, arm tube radius), surface detail and decorative counts (the four feet, the 22 rack teeth, the 18 pinion teeth) count toward neither, per VISUAL_DIVERSITY_MODEL.

MULTIPLICITY: NONE, AND NONE IS INVENTED. `multiplicities` is deliberately empty. No record in the pool contains a repeated structural member under a count parameter. The four rubber feet (ORIGIN L142-L150) are a fixed decorative count on a single part. The 22 rack teeth (var_rack L56) and 18 pinion teeth (L278) are internal to one candidate's own CAD solid, not a slot that could be instantiated N times, so they are candidate parameters (rack_tooth_count, pinion_teeth) rather than a multiplicity. Inventing an N here would inflate raw_domain without adding a single new assembly relationship, which is exactly what VISUAL_DIVERSITY_MODEL forbids.

CROSS-SLOT RISKS, AND WHY DERIVATION RATHER THAN GATING RESOLVES EACH.
(a) The head's pivot width drives the post's fork spacing. fork_y_m = pivot_drum_length_m/2 + fork_thickness_m/2 and crossbar_y_m >= 2*(fork_y_m + fork_thickness_m/2), verified across five records with no exception. rectangular_enclosed_hood is the proof it is live: widening the hood widened the drum to 0.060, which moved the forks to 0.034, which widened the crossbar to 0.078. Any post candidate therefore fits any head candidate because the post reads the head's interface dimension instead of assuming one.
(b) Mast retention is a two-pose rule, not a single fit. sleeve_length_m - mast_stroke_m >= 0.075 comes from a POSED assertion (ORIGIN L595-L605), not the rest pose, so stroke and sleeve length can never be parameterised independently. resolve_config clamps mast_stroke_effective_m rather than rejecting the pair.
(c) The stage frame adapts to the mast in BOTH directions. single_telescoping_mast and folding_cantilever_mast UNION a land (0.060x0.052 and 0.060x0.066); twin_column_mast CUTS a 0.026x0.086x0.014 relief. The rebuild derives which and its footprint from mast_section_y_m against a 0.048 threshold - the three land/none sections are 0.028-0.030 and the relief section is 0.064, so the classification has 16 mm of margin on both sides. Hard-coding either direction would break half the slot.
(d) folding_cantilever_mast moves the head joint origin to x = head_offset_x_m (-0.070 in the source) together with its beam and its forks. That single derivation moves the head, the mirror, the mirror's stage clearance and the whole optical stack-up. It is authored as head_joint_x_m in binding head_drum_to_post_fork and consumed by optical_stackup_stage_clearance.
(e) Slots A and C BOTH write into lift_post. They compose because they act on different axes of the same member: slot A owns the fork X width and Y spacing plus the crossbar profile and the mast section; slot C owns the fork HEIGHT and centre Z (0.050 short capture forks -> 0.140 slide rails -> 190 mm guide cheeks with a cut circle(0.0055) shaft bore) and whether the crossbar sits at the joint plane (rack) or 0.031 below it (everything else). No pair of slot-A and slot-C candidates conflicts; there is no gate and none is needed.
(f) Mirror trunnions are SEATED, never coincident and never merely tangent. boss_outer_face_y_m = socket_inner_face_y_m + part_contact_embed_m, so the boss end face is driven 0.3 mm past the socket end face. swiveling_mirror_yoke supplies the geometry and proves it needs zero allowances of either kind; the 0.3 mm is the rebuild's own addition, because MECHANICAL_PRIORS 1c (rewritten) rejects an exact part-to-part kiss as fragile. part_contact_embed_m is a single named derived value used at all six cross-part seats (collar/sleeve, drum/fork, carrier/head, trunnion/socket, rocker/bezel, knob/shaft) and at none of the running fits.

ALLOW_OVERLAP: TWO RECORDS USE IT, THE REBUILD USES NONE. preflight BLOCKS ctx.allow_overlap outright for Design-backed templates (AUTHORING.md section 5) and re-checks the actual emitted allowances in the author-test report, so indirection through a helper or alias is also caught. mirror_motion_fold_flat_mirror has 4 sites (L599, L606, L629, L636), hiding hinge bosses moved to |y|=0.060 that land exactly on the socket CENTRES. mirror_motion_dual_hinge_mirror has 5 sites (L460, L467, L474, L481, L488), hiding a swivel pin driven into the head arm and trunnions driven through both yoke cheeks into the socket bores. Both are papering over a construction the pool elsewhere gets right: the remaining 9 records - including swiveling_mirror_yoke, which builds the same two-axis mechanism - use ZERO allowances. The rebuild therefore (i) derives boss_y_m tangentially for all four mirror candidates via binding mirror_trunnion_tangency with a deliberate 0.3 mm seat overlap, and (ii) WELDS the dual-hinge swivel pin's seat into the projection_head solid as one part, because intra-part embedding is free (MECHANICAL_PRIORS 1c - collisions are computed part-to-part only). allow_isolated_part is not used anywhere in this pool and should not be needed: every moving member here has a real seated contact.

CONSTRUCTION RULE - WELD INERT DRESSING INTO THE HOUSING SOLID. sdk/_core/v0/exact_collisions.py derives one collision solid per VISUAL, 1:1. The origin's body part emits about 20 separate primitive visuals (molded housing, lower lamp housing, access panel + pull, stage frame, fresnel plate + 2 registration marks, side vent, 4 feet, cable grommet, cable relief, post bracket, post sleeve, lock shaft, switch bezel), which would become about 20 collision bodies on a part that never moves. The rebuild unions the structurally-inert dressing (access panel and pull, fresnel registration marks, switch bezel, the four feet, the cable grommet, the post bracket, the lock shaft) into the housing CAD solid, and keeps a separate visual only where a distinct material is load-bearing for recognizability: the translucent glass stage, the slot-pattern side vent, the cable relief tail, and the post sleeve. That cuts the body from about 20 collision solids to about 6 while preserving every visible feature. It is safe precisely because the welded features are all on the same part.

PART TREE. projector_body (root, the only grounded part; every record asserts len(root_parts()) == 1) -> lift_post on the prismatic height_adjust -> projection_head on the head joint (revolute for folding_tilt, prismatic for the two focus slides) -> mirror, either directly or through mirror_yoke on a (0,0,1) swivel. power_switch and lock_knob hang off projector_body directly. Seeds therefore carry 5 parts and 5 joints for the two single-hinge mirror candidates, and 6 parts and 6 joints for the two two-axis ones. Diagnosable entity names follow <slot>__<candidate>__<local_name>.

MIRROR REST ANGLE LIVES IN THE JOINT, NOT THE VISUAL. The origin bakes rpy=(0,-0.65,0) into two mirror visuals (L335, L341); fold_flat_mirror moves it into the joint origin (L382). The rebuild always uses the joint, because a parameterised mirror angle has to re-derive the fold-flat limit with it (fold_flat_stop_rad = -mirror_rest_angle_rad) and because q=0 should mean 'deployed' in every candidate.

derived.expression: sleeve_bore_r_m if post_section == 'round_single' else (sleeve_bore_r_m if post_section == 'twin_round' else min(sleeve_bore_x_m, sleeve_bore_y_m) / 2.0)
derived.name: mast_sleeve_bore_half_m
derived.rationale: Smallest half-dimension of the sleeve bore, whatever section the candidate builds. Round 0.0097 (ORIGIN L48), twin 0.0097 per column (var_twin L70), rect_single min(0.026, 0.020)/2 = 0.010 (var_single L63) and min(0.024, 0.018)/2 = 0.009 (var_cantilever L58).

derived.expression: post_r_m if post_section in ('round_single', 'twin_round') else min(mast_x_m, mast_y_m) / 2.0
derived.name: mast_shank_half_m
derived.rationale: Matching half-dimension of the moving mast. Round/twin 0.0085 (ORIGIN L206, var_twin L90); rect 0.009 (var_single L73) and 0.008 (var_cantilever L218).

derived.name: mast_running_clearance_m
derived.rationale: The pool's running fit: 0.0012 for the round and twin candidates (0.0097 - 0.0085), 0.0010 for both rectangular ones. ORIGIN L538-L546 asserts it as expect_within(inner_post subset post_sleeve, axes='xy', margin=0.0). Must stay strictly positive or the mast cannot slide.

derived.name: sleeve_base_z_m
derived.rationale: World Z of the sleeve bottom. ORIGIN L185 places it at 0.155 against a stage frame whose top is 0.171 + 0.004 = 0.175; the 0.016 drop lets the sleeve foot reach through the frame plane into the bracket.

derived.name: sleeve_top_z_m
derived.rationale: World Z of the sleeve top and therefore of the height_adjust joint origin. ORIGIN: 0.155 + 0.200 = 0.355, which is exactly the joint origin at L241 and exactly where the stop_collar bottom lands (SourceMap mating rule 4). One source of truth for three things.

derived.name: mast_insertion_rest_m
derived.rationale: Overlap between mast and sleeve at rest. ORIGIN: sleeve spans world 0.155..0.355, the post spans 0.195..0.575, so the insertion is 0.160 and L547-L555 asserts min_overlap=0.150.

derived.name: mast_insertion_extended_m
derived.rationale: Insertion at the top of the stroke. ORIGIN: 0.160 - 0.080 = 0.080, asserted min_overlap=0.075 INSIDE a posed block at L595-L605. This is the pose that actually constrains the design.

derived.name: mast_retention_floor_m
derived.rationale: The retention floor the pool asserts (ORIGIN L604). MATING RULE 1: the real constraint is sleeve_length_m - mast_stroke_m >= 0.075, which is why stroke and sleeve length can NEVER be sampled independently. resolve_config clamps mast_stroke_m to min(mast_stroke_m, sleeve_length_m - 0.075) rather than rejecting the combination - there are no gates in TemplateDomain.

derived.name: mast_stroke_effective_m
derived.rationale: The stroke actually written into the prismatic joint's upper limit. At the authored extremes (sleeve 0.150, stroke 0.110) this clamps to 0.075; at the pool values (0.200, 0.080) it is 0.080 unchanged.

derived.name: part_contact_embed_m
derived.rationale: THE ONE DELIBERATE PART-TO-PART OVERLAP OF THIS TEMPLATE, and the reason no seated contact in the rebuild is authored as exact tangency. MECHANICAL_PRIORS section 1c: collisions are computed part-to-part only, so a contact that is EXACTLY tangent is the fragile case - CadQuery may keep two tangent solids separate, triangulation can open the seam, and the connectivity tolerance is 1e-6. A seated contact between two different parts must therefore carry an explicit, named overlap rather than a zero gap. 0.0003 m is sized against find_geometry_overlaps' 1e-3 m overlap_tol (and the 0.005 m env default, which is looser still), so it registers as contact and never as a collision, while staying under a tenth of the smallest seated feature in the pool (the 0.005 m spherical trunnion boss of ORIGIN L346) so it is invisible at the 0.35 m category scale. It is deliberately NOT applied to running fits: the mast/sleeve clearance (mast_running_clearance_m), the rack_and_pinion carriage clearance and the pinion mesh gap all stay real gaps. Applied at exactly six cross-part seats: stop_collar on the sleeve top, drum end faces in the fork inner faces, the mirror carrier on its head seat, the mirror trunnions in their sockets, the rocker on its bezel and the lock knob on its shaft end.

derived.name: stop_collar_seat_z_m
derived.rationale: Where the stop collar's bottom face lands. ORIGIN L212-L213: collar centre at post-local 0.004 with height 0.008 -> bottom at post-local 0.0, i.e. exactly the joint origin, i.e. exactly the sleeve top. ORIGIN L530-L537 asserts contact at 0.0015. The rebuild seats it part_contact_embed_m INTO the sleeve top rather than exactly on it: lift_post and projector_body are different parts, so per MECHANICAL_PRIORS 1c the seat needs a deliberate overlap. The collar still lifts clear for every stroke > part_contact_embed_m, which is what a stop collar does.

derived.name: post_section
derived.rationale: Which section family the active mast candidate builds. Carried as a derived value so the sleeve, the bracket, the stage adaptation and the lock shaft all read one source of truth instead of four independent branches.

derived.expression: 2.0 * sleeve_outer_r_m if post_section == 'round_single' else (sleeve_web_x_m if post_section == 'twin_round' else sleeve_outer_x_m)
derived.name: mast_section_x_m
derived.rationale: X footprint of the sleeve. ORIGIN 0.028 (2 x 0.014, L47); var_twin 0.028 (the web, L65); var_single 0.034 (L58); var_cantilever 0.036 (L55).

derived.expression: 2.0 * sleeve_outer_r_m if post_section == 'round_single' else (2.0 * (column_offset_m + sleeve_outer_r_m) if post_section == 'twin_round' else sleeve_outer_y_m)
derived.name: mast_section_y_m
derived.rationale: Y footprint of the sleeve, and THE input to the whole host adaptation. ORIGIN 0.028; var_twin 2*(0.018+0.014) = 0.064 (L53/L57); var_single 0.028 (L58); var_cantilever 0.030 (L55). The twin candidate is more than twice as wide as the others, which is exactly why it needs a different adaptation.

derived.name: post_bracket_y_m
derived.rationale: Body-side bracket width. Reproduces all four records exactly: ORIGIN 0.028 + 2*0.014 = 0.056 (L178); var_single 0.028 + 2*0.016 = 0.060 (L211); var_twin 0.064 + 2*0.009 = 0.082 (L231); var_cantilever 0.030 + 2*0.015 = 0.060 (L190). var_twin's own author test L577-L590 asserts bracket Y >= 0.080.

derived.name: stage_host_adaptation
derived.rationale: MATING RULE 5, AND IT GOES BOTH WAYS. var_single and var_cantilever UNION a land onto the stage frame; var_twin CUTS a relief out of it. The rebuild decides from the mast section rather than hard-coding one: a section that fits beside the frame rail gets a load-transferring land, a section too wide to fit displaces frame material and gets a relief. Both are local adaptations of an unchanged square host, which is what AUTHORING.md section 4 asks for.

derived.name: stage_relief_threshold_y_m
derived.rationale: The section width above which a land becomes a relief. Authored, and bounded by the pool on both sides: the three land/none candidates have sections of 0.028, 0.028 and 0.030, the relief candidate has 0.064. 0.048 is the midpoint of that gap and no pool value is within 16 mm of it, so the classification is robust across the full parameter ranges.

derived.name: stage_frame_edge_x_m
derived.rationale: Outer X edge of the stage frame. ORIGIN L41 + L100: a 0.310-wide frame centred at x=-0.015 -> edge at 0.140. The land is the bridge from this edge out to the mast.

derived.name: stage_frame_rail_m
derived.rationale: Width of the frame rail. ORIGIN L41-L43: (0.310 - 0.286)/2 = 0.012.

derived.name: stage_mast_pad_x_m
derived.rationale: X footprint of the land or relief. LAND: it bridges from the frame edge out to the sleeve's outer face - var_single (0.185+0.017) - 0.140 = 0.062 against an authored 0.060 (L48), var_cantilever (0.185+0.018) - 0.140 = 0.063 against 0.060 (L47); both records rounded to a 5 mm grid, the expression is within 3 mm and moves correctly with the station. RELIEF: it must straddle the whole rail - var_twin 0.012 + 0.014 = 0.026, exactly L46.

derived.name: stage_mast_pad_y_m
derived.rationale: Y footprint. LAND: var_single 0.028 + 2*0.012 = 0.052 exactly (L48); var_cantilever 0.030 + 2*0.018 = 0.066 exactly (L47). RELIEF: it must clear the BRACKET, not the sleeve - var_twin 0.082 + 2*0.002 = 0.086, exactly L46. That asymmetry is the point: material you add only has to carry the mast, material you remove has to clear everything that passes through.

derived.name: stage_mast_pad_h_m
derived.rationale: Height of the land or the depth of the relief. LAND: flush with the 0.008 frame (var_single L48, var_cantilever L47). RELIEF: 0.014 against a 0.008 frame (var_twin L46) - deliberately deeper so it is a clean through-cut with no coincident faces.

derived.name: stage_mast_pad_station_x_m
derived.rationale: Centre X of the land/relief. Land: 0.140 + 0.031 = 0.171 against var_single's 0.170 (L49). Relief: 0.140 - 0.006 = 0.134 against var_twin's 0.151 (L47); the record biases the cut outward, the expression centres it on the rail it has to remove, which is the more robust rule when the station moves.

derived.name: stage_mast_pad_station_y_m
derived.rationale: Centre Y of the land/relief. The pool biases it slightly inboard (0.115 for var_single L49, 0.107 for var_cantilever L48, 0.105 for var_twin L47) but the footprints derived above cover the sleeve and bracket from the station in every case, so the rebuild centres on the station and drops the 0-10 mm bias.

derived.name: stage_frame_outer_x_m
derived.rationale: Stage frame outer X. ORIGIN L41: box(0.310, 0.280, 0.008), identical in all 11 records including the three that modify the function.

derived.name: stage_frame_opening_x_m
derived.rationale: Stage frame opening X, genuinely cut. ORIGIN L42: box(0.286, 0.256, 0.012). MECHANICAL_PRIORS section 7 - the bordered frame around a translucent plate is structure, not dressing.

derived.name: stage_frame_thickness_m
derived.rationale: Stage frame thickness. ORIGIN L41.

derived.name: stage_frame_centre_x_m
derived.rationale: Stage frame placement X. ORIGIN L100: origin (-0.015, -0.004, 0.171).

derived.name: stage_frame_top_z_m
derived.rationale: Top of the glass stage: frame at z=0.171 (ORIGIN L100) plus the 0.004 fresnel plate at 0.172 (L106). This is the datum the >=0.42 m mirror clearance anchor measures from.

derived.name: fork_y_m
derived.rationale: MATING RULE 2, verified across five records with no exception: ORIGIN drum0.052 -> fork y 0.030 (L225/L231); var_round_lamp 0.052 -> 0.030 (L249/L255); var_hood 0.060 -> 0.034 (L239/L245); var_sliding 0.052 -> 0.030 (L239/L245); var_twin 0.052 -> 0.030. The head's own pivot width drives the post's fork spacing. This is the binding the SourceMap calls out as PROVEN live, because widening the hood widened the drum, which moved the forks, which widened the crossbar. The rule is kept exactly, minus the named part_contact_embed_m: projection_head and lift_post are different parts, so the capture is authored as a deliberate 0.3 mm interference rather than the source's exact kiss (MECHANICAL_PRIORS 1c).

derived.name: fork_inner_y_m
derived.rationale: Y of each fork's inner face - pivot_drum_length_m/2 minus part_contact_embed_m. ORIGIN 0.026, var_hood 0.030, both with the drum end face EXACTLY on the fork inner face; the rebuild moves the fork 0.3 mm inboard so the drum end is genuinely captured rather than tangent. expect_contact(pivot_drum, head_fork_0, contact_tol=0.0015) still passes with zero allowance (ORIGIN L556-L563), and the 0.3 mm interference is an order of magnitude below find_geometry_overlaps' 1e-3 overlap_tol. The interference is along the head's own pivot axis, so it is invariant under both the revolute fold and the prismatic focus travel.

derived.name: fork_outer_y_m
derived.rationale: Y of each fork's outer face. ORIGIN 0.034, var_hood 0.038.

derived.name: fork_capture_span_y_m
derived.rationale: Clear span between the forks, which must equal the drum length exactly. This is the axis interface capacity the head consumes.

derived.name: crossbar_y_m
derived.rationale: SECOND HALF OF MATING RULE 2: crossbar_Y >= 2*(fork_y + fork_thickness/2). ORIGIN max(0.068 + 0.002, 0 + 0.024) = 0.070 exactly (L218); var_hood max(0.076 + 0.002, ...) = 0.078 exactly (L232); var_twin max(0.070, 0.054 + 0.024) = 0.078 exactly (L270) - the twin candidate's crossbar is wider because its upper bridge, not its drum, sets the floor. Two independent providers, one max(); no gate needed.

derived.name: mast_head_bridge_y_m
derived.rationale: The mast's own contribution to the crossbar width floor. Only the twin-column candidate has an upper bridge to accommodate (var_twin L101: 0.054).

derived.name: head_joint_x_m
derived.rationale: THE CANTILEVER BINDING, and a real one. var_cantilever moves BOTH forks to x=-0.070 (L237/L243) AND the head_tilt joint origin to (-0.070, 0, 0.255) (L337). The beam carries the forks; the joint has to travel with them or the head hangs off nothing. Every other mast candidate leaves it at 0.0 (ORIGIN L325). This is a derivation, not a cosmetic offset: it moves the head, the mirror, the mirror's stage clearance and the whole optical stack-up with it.

derived.name: head_carrier_x_m
derived.rationale: Centre X of the crossbar-or-beam. var_cantilever L231 places the 0.095-long beam at x=-0.036, i.e. roughly half the fork offset, so the beam spans from the mast centreline out to the forks. Plain crossbars sit on the centreline.

derived.name: head_carrier_x_len_m
derived.rationale: X length of the crossbar-or-beam. 0.050 for the plain crossbar in ORIGIN L218, var_hood L232 and var_twin L270; 0.095 for the cantilever beam (L230). Must reach at least |head_joint_x_m| + post_fork_width_x_m/2 so the forks are supported along their whole footprint.

derived.name: crossbar_profile
derived.rationale: Which crossbar the head candidate forces on the post. var_round_lamp L242 replaces the 0.050x0.070x0.012 box with a Cylinder(r=0.012, len=0.070) rotated about X. A second host adaptation driven purely by the head slot, and one that composes with the cantilever beam (a round beam at an offset is still a round beam).

derived.name: crossbar_z_m
derived.rationale: Crossbar centre height. ORIGIN 0.255 - 0.031 = 0.224 (L219), same in var_round_lamp L243, var_hood L233, var_sliding L233, var_twin L271. The rack_and_pinion candidate is the exception: its crossbar IS the 190 mm rack and it sits ON the joint plane at 0.255 (var_rack L246), because the rack has to span the whole travel.

derived.name: drum_effective_r_m
derived.rationale: Radius of the drum as built. 0.021 for folding_tilt with any head (ORIGIN L249, var_hood L263); 0.015 for sliding_lens_barrel (var_sliding L263 = 0.021 - 0.006), because once the forks become slide rails the drum is a slider block, not a trunnion. rack_and_pinion has no drum at all - see focus_motion_to_post_rails.

derived.name: fork_capture_r_m
derived.rationale: Radius of the capture envelope the forks must cover. Feeds the axis interface the post publishes; ORIGIN's own check runs at contact_tol=0.0015 (L562).

derived.name: head_joint_kind
derived.rationale: The head joint's TYPE is the focus candidate, and nothing else in the category changes joint type (SourceMap category anchor 3). REVOLUTE (0,1,0) for folding_tilt (ORIGIN L320-L329); PRISMATIC (0,0,1) for both slides (var_sliding L334-L344, var_rack L363-L373).

derived.name: head_joint_axis_vec
derived.rationale: Carried explicitly so register_interface_mate and the anchor check read one value. No joint anywhere in this pool uses any other axis.

derived.expression: head_fork_height_m if focus == 'folding_tilt' else (rail_length_m if focus == 'sliding_lens_barrel' else rack_length_m)
derived.name: fork_height_m
derived.rationale: THE SLOT-A/SLOT-C COMPOSITION. Both slots write into lift_post: slot A owns the fork X width and Y spacing, slot C owns their HEIGHT. 0.050-0.054 short capture forks for folding_tilt (ORIGIN L224, var_round_lamp L248); 0.140 slide rails for sliding_lens_barrel (var_sliding L238); 0.190 guide cheeks for rack_and_pinion (var_rack L68). The two host adaptations compose because they act on different axes of the same member.

derived.name: fork_centre_z_m
derived.rationale: Centre height of the forks/rails. ORIGIN 0.255 (L225); var_sliding 0.255 + 0.025 = 0.280 (L239) because the carriage travels upward and the rails have to lead it; var_rack 0.255 (L253), centred because its travel is symmetric (-0.055..+0.055).

derived.name: fork_bore_required
derived.rationale: MECHANICAL_PRIORS section 7. The rack_and_pinion pinion shaft passes THROUGH both guide cheeks, so var_rack L69-L75 cuts a real circle(0.0055) passage in each cheek rather than notching it or floating the shaft. No other focus candidate has a member crossing the forks.

derived.name: shaft_bore_clearance_m
derived.rationale: 0.0055 - 0.004 = 0.0015 in var_rack (L72 vs L286). Must stay positive so the shaft turns inside a cut bore instead of intersecting the cheek solid.

derived.name: focus_shaft_len_m
derived.rationale: Shaft length, re-derived from the fork spacing so it always reaches through both cheek bores and out to the knob. var_rack L286: 0.078 against forks whose outer faces are at |y| = 0.034 and a 0.014-long knob at y=-0.046 (L293). Any change to pivot_drum_length_m moves the forks, so this length must follow.

derived.name: focus_knob_len_m
derived.rationale: Focus knob length. var_rack L292.

derived.name: pinion_pitch_r_m
derived.rationale: SpurGear pitch radius. var_rack L278: 0.002 * 18 / 2 = 0.018. The mesh line is derived from this, so changing the tooth count re-seats the pinion instead of burying it in the rack.

derived.name: rack_tooth_tip_x_m
derived.rationale: X of the tooth tips facing the carriage. var_rack L55/L60: a 0.012-wide bar with 0.009-wide teeth translated to x=-0.0105 -> tips at -0.015.

derived.name: pinion_tip_r_m
derived.rationale: Addendum circle of the SpurGear: pitch radius plus one module (the SDK SpurGear default addendum_coeff is 1.0). var_rack L278: 0.018 + 0.002 = 0.020. This, not the pitch circle, is the radius that actually touches the rack.

derived.name: pinion_centre_x_m
derived.rationale: Where the pinion sits. var_rack L281 places it at -0.034 against tips at -0.015 and a 0.018 pitch radius: pitch circle 0.001 clear of the tips, i.e. the 0.020 ADDENDUM circle 0.001 INTO them - a real mesh, exactly as MECHANICAL_PRIORS section 4 requires (tangent or meshed, never a bulk overlap), and with no allowance.
